label: miso 42 coal econ
definition: MISO 42 (CANDIDATE, L-14 G-23 lever; keeper stays miso-41 pending owner call): miso-41 recipe + coal_econ_srmc_bound — the marginal (econ*/peak) coal tranches' fuel passthrough is clamped to >=1.0 so no marginal coal offer sits below the plant's measured F923 incremental delivered SRMC; the committed/must-run bands keep the contracted take-or-pay discount. Removes the passthrough sigmoid's fitted discount from tranches whose fuel is bought at market (FINDING-miso-burndown-2026-07.md Evidence 2: model LMP sat $4-5 below the cheapest measured coal tranche while coal was marginal ~94% of hours) — a DOF reduction, nothing tuned. RESULT vs miso-41: the priced-out classes wake up structurally (ST_GAS 2.9/3.3/3.4 -> 6.8/7.3/5.3 TWh; CT_PEAKER 13.4/17.3/16.9 -> 15.0/20.8/17.6; net imports 14.7/3.7/-5.1 -> 19.5/6.3/-4.6 vs actual 37.9/23.1/19.0); C3a improves all 3 years (-8.2/-13.0/-18.9% vs -9.8/-15.6/-19.5%); 2025 coal over-run improves (C2 +7.2% vs +8.8%); CO2 PASS x3; legitimacy D-gates Overall PASS (C7/C8 PASS, zero forced energy from the bound — it is an offer bound, not a floor). COSTS: coal 2023/24 under-run deepens (154.9/144.2 vs actual 175.0/167.1 — the sigmoid discount was silently compensating for missing coal self-commitment volume; the committed band is not yet sized from the measured EIA-923 Sch-5 contract share in the MISO fleet branch) and CC_REGULAR worsens +2.9/+4.3/+1.8 to +46.4/+46.8 TWh (2023/24) — confirming per FINDING-miso-cc-decomposition-2026-07.md that the CC row is the P1 commitment-posture wedge (DP-1: +34% committed CC energy vs MIP; 135.6x1.34=181.7~=model), designed (not built) in docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-posture-design-2026-07.md. C3c tail still 0 h (needs the posture lever). C5b 2025 (+1296.7%) is a benchmark basis artifact, not a model miss — EIA-930 MISO reports battery-only while the model side includes the 2,417 MW PS fleet whose throughput matches the eGRID net-energy-implied band (FINDING-miso-c5b-storage-benchmark-2026-07.md).
